Author: mobolajiadewale

  • INTRUSION

     The home is a home until it isn’t,
    Etched in the brain like malignant cankers,
    This suffering in soul doesn’t yield or wither,
    The pain felt too deep to be physical or whole.
    Just sore, and grey, and scarring its soldiers,
    This war once waged to reclaim a hearth,
    This home now a nightmare,
    This home lost its laugh.
    Should one say when it happened,
    Or so suspects when it changed,
    That night, on that weekend, when the world seemed unruly,
    Bathing in bliss and fighting fear’s folds.
    Returned to see carnage,
    A bloodbath,
    Brought tears.
    The home is a home if you fight off invaders,
    Yet the stench lingers clean, glued to walls and dulled papers,
    This home now a nightmare,
    This home now a farce,
    This home now unsafe,
    Fools the fool, this façade.
    August 12, 2025

  • ɟןǝs

    Ive been in love,

    With my self,

    And self-image,

    All-consuming,

    Time-wasting,

    Pestilent and wasteful,

    But I can’t shake it,

    Or break it,

    Or make it,

    From the self-gratifying slump that Dorian himself also tackled,

    The harder I try to remove my self-worth, the larger it becomes,

    Like the blots of sin and wretched hideousness of Gray’s portrait,

    I am at my wits end,

    Unable to fathom a world in which the self does not admire itself and the being does not suppose themselves supreme in all matters concerning their own loves,

    For the feeling of sonder is so fleeting it barely registers to affect the psyche I have built,

    Built without conscious effort or tribulation,

    I have love for myself and far too much of it,

    But it is better than the latter,

    For that would be the death of me.

    April 6, 2021

  • ʇǝod

    Im not poet,

    Or writer,

    Or orator,

    Simply a man,

    Once a child,

    Grown in a world of social phenomena and mass media,

    With no access to a past before it,

    Except through the escapes of musicality and culture,

    All of which are found on the very devices thought impossible in the times I venture to in my dreams,

    I am unfortunate to be unable to move through time,

    Temporally shifting my way through eras and eons of cultural upheaval,

    But I then look at myself and think,

    There is no greater time for me than the present,

    With dark skin and dark eyes,

    Dark clothes and dark skies,

    The best time for me is now,

    Any dive into the past would end in shackles, death, or vagrancy,

    And I would not survive the latter,

    I am thankful to be alive now,

    And thankful that nostalgia is so painfully blissful,

    The escapes comfort me but ground me at the same time,

    And stop me from repeating the same rhymes,

    Im not poet,

    Or writer,

    Or orator,

    Simply a man,

    Living in a time I am thankful to call my own.

    April 6, 2021

  • Meal

    The stove burned with a rage, hotter than the Sun itself,
And with splendid glory it roared,
Like a great daemon, anticipating its victim,
The victim was the pan, that fell onto the metallic slabs with a shudder.
The sweet glow of the bean on the stove left much to the imagination,
As the child's lips beamed open with an ingrained efficiency,
Soon, he would be devouring his meal, with devilish menace,
But for now, he waited, and watched as the flame ripped through the layers of metal, holding the pan in place.
    April 21, 2020

  • Argonne

    Their black on black eyes elucidated the hellish world that they drowned in,

Only the catatonic should see those spectres: for they do not react, just lay in their suffering.

Ares championed it, as did they, the crude alpacas who sat on chairs, shouting through pressed mahogany, into the ears of men half dead,

But death was normal, and it's god was still lustful, forcing its gluttony upon a canvas of châteaus and campagne,

Yet still, those black on black eyes elucidated their hell, their suffering from which there was no return,

Their end, their loss, their defeat, their circle of hell, reserved based on their heinous crimes to Gaia,

and to the descendants of Noah himself a mark so feared it mirrored that of Cains, a simple cross,

Not awarded for valiance but instead for ruinous efficiency: at smiting ones foes and ripping their once hot lives from their now cold, hard hands.

All the while smiling. Laughing, losing oneself, expunging their own humanities while removing those of their foes.

The Irony.
    April 21, 2020

  • Crimson

    A sea of red flushed through the room,
Followed by a dark cacophony of smells,
Nauseating in nature, lustful in depth.
I stood where they stood, screaming as they did,
A naïve Noah, peering into Hell with eyes wide open,
Orifices shut,
Gazing at a glimpse of a world far different to my own,
Far worse than my own,
Flooded with a deep, demon sea,
That ripped through flesh and bubbled lungs,
That mangled eyes and hair alike,
That welded guns to digits,
That killed unceremoniously,
That killed me,
Killed my mind,
Murdered my soul,
Ravaged by skin,
All in the name of war,
For a nation I did not belong.
    April 20, 2020
